title: Fluorescent Protein Production, Purification, and Coupling to Microspheres
protocol: Express mPlum-pBAD FP in One Shot TOP10 electrocompetent E. coli cells.
Purify the expressed mPlum construct using immobilized metal affinity chromatography (IMAC).
Further purify the sample by size exclusion chromatography (SEC).
Evaluate the purity of the sample by SEC and sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE).
Check for a predominant protein band at an expected molecular weight of 29.5 kDa on SDS-PAGE.
Ensure the presence of a single, symmetrical peak with an elution volume >50 ml on SEC.
Prepare plasmid DNA using the Qiagen Plus Maxi Kit according to the manufacturer's instructions for mPlum-pBAD.
Place One Shot TOP10 electrocompetent E. coli cells in an electroporation cuvette and add approximately 100 ng of DNA.
Activate the electroporation unit and pulse for the designated time.
Plate cells on an LB agar plate supplemented with 2% glucose and 100 µg/ml ampicillin and incubate at 37°C for 24 hr to allow recovery.
Pick a single colony from the transformed plate and inoculate into 300 ml LB medium supplemented with 2% glucose and 100 µg/ml ampicillin in a 2-L baffled flask to form a starter culture.
Incubate starter culture at 37°C for 18 hr with shaking at 120 rpm.
Determine OD600 of starter culture using a spectrophotometer.
Calculate the amount of starter culture required to inoculate an expression culture to an OD600 of 0.075 using C1V1 = C2V2 equation.
Inoculate 1 L LB medium supplemented with 0.2% glucose and 100 µg/ml ampicillin with the calculated amount of starter culture in a 2-L baffled flask.
Incubate expression culture at 37°C with shaking at 120 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.6.
Add 20% (w/v) L-arabinose to expression culture to achieve a final concentration of 0.2% (v/v).
Incubate expression culture overnight at 37°C with shaking at 120 rpm.
Pour the expression culture into 1-L centrifuge bottles and harvest cells by centrifugation for 15 min at 13,000 × g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant from harvested cells and transfer cell pellets to 50-ml centrifuge tubes.
Freeze down cell pellets to −80°C to aid with bacterial lysis.
Prepare cold cell lysis buffer.
Thaw cell pellets on ice and add 40 ml fresh cold cell lysis buffer per liter of expression culture supplemented with one cOmplete Protease Inhibitor tablet and a few grains of DNase I.
Gently swirl the mixture every minute for 10 min at room temperature to mix cell lysate.
Disrupt cells by sonication using 40% amplitude, pulsating for 10 seconds on and off for a total of 10 minutes.
Keep lysate cold during sonication by performing the process on ice.
Clarify lysate by centrifuging at 40,000 × g for 40 minutes at 4°C.
Filter clear lysate into a 1-L Schott bottle using a 0.22-μm syringe filter.
Prepare a 1-ml IMAC column according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Apply cleared filtered lysate onto an IMAC column at 1 ml/min using a peristaltic pump, collecting flow-through in a new 1-L Schott bottle.
Apply flow-through from step 23 onto the same IMAC column at 1 ml/min and collect flow-through in another new 1-L Schott bottle.
Prepare IMAC elution buffer according to the specified recipe.
Plumb the IMAC column onto the Bio-Rad NGC Quest 10 Plus medium-pressure liquid chromatography system.
Fill Buffer A reservoir with cell lysis buffer and Buffer B reservoir with IMAC elution buffer.
Wash IMAC column using 15 column volumes of cell lysis buffer.
Elute protein of interest using a gradient from 0% to 100% IMAC elution buffer over 20 column volumes.
Collect samples from fractionated peaks displayed on the Bio-Rad NGC Quest 10 Plus software and run them on a 4%-12% Mini-PROTEAN TGX Stain-Free Precast Gel under reduced and denatured conditions.
Store fractions at 4°C until use.
Pool fractions containing the protein of interest.
Concentrate the pooled fractions to 5 ml using a 10-kDa-cutoff centrifuge filter according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Plumb a HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 75 pg SEC column onto the Bio-Rad NGC Quest 10 Plus system.
Equilibrate the SEC column with DPBS.
Load 5 ml of concentrated pooled fraction onto the SEC column using a 5-ml manual load loop.
Resolve the protein of interest on the SEC column using 1.2 column volumes.
Collect fractionated peaks and run on SDS-PAGE to identify the protein of interest.
Pool fractions containing the protein of interest.
Add glycerol to the pooled fractions to achieve a final concentration of 10%.
Concentrate the protein to between 2 and 4 mg/ml using a 10-kDa-cutoff centrifuge filter.
Determine the concentration of the protein by measuring A280 and dividing it by the extinction coefficient of the protein.
Aliquot the protein into 250-µg lots.
Flash-freeze the aliquots in liquid nitrogen.
Store at -80°C until use.
Resuspend the 4.5-μm carboxylate microspheres by inverting the bottle multiple times or vortexing vigorously.
Pipette 0.5 ml bead suspension into a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 × g.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in 0.5 ml PolyLink coupling buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 × g.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in 0.17 ml PolyLink coupling buffer.
Prepare 10 mg EDAC in 50 µl PolyLink coupling buffer.
Add 20 µl of the EDAC solution to the bead suspension and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Vortex briefly then add 250 µg purified FP suspended in 100 μl of 90% (v/v) DPBS and 10% (v/v) glycerol.
Incubate for 4 hr on a rotary mixer at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 × g.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in 0.5 ml PolyLink storage buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 × g.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in 1 ml PolyLink storage buffer.
Add 50 µl bead suspension to a 5-ml dropper bottle.
Add 4 ml DPBS with 0.02% sodium azide to the dropper bottle.
Prepare blank beads by diluting 25 µl stock beads with 4 ml DPBS, 0.02% sodium azide, and 2% BSA.
Store beads for at least 1 year at 4°C.
Perform unmixing using FP-coupled beads on the Cytek Aurora instrument.
Acquire single FP-expressing cells on the instrument after unmixing.
Export median fluorescence intensities (MFIs) from all fluorescence channels to Excel™ or other graphing software.
Subtract values from negative particles from those for positive particles to isolate FP values regardless of autofluorescence.
Resuspend the 4.5-µm polystyrene microspheres with no FP (blank beads) by inverting the bottle multiple times or vortexing vigorously.
Dispense one drop of blank beads into a 12 × 75–mm polystyrene test tube (∼40 µl).
Add 200 µl DPBS to the test tube containing blank beads.
Resuspend the 4.5-µm polystyrene microspheres coupled to FP by inverting the bottle multiple times or vortexing vigorously.
Dispense one drop of FP-coupled beads into a 12 × 75–mm polystyrene test tube (∼40 µl).
Add 200 µl DPBS to the test tube containing FP-coupled beads.
Add 200 µl non-FP-expressing parental cells (unstained cells) to a 12 × 75–mm test tube (∼50,000 cells).
Add 200 µl FP-expressing cells to a 12 × 75–mm test tube (∼50,000 cells).
Open SpectroFlo software and choose “default experiment.”
Install the tube of blank beads in the Cytek Aurora spectral cytometer and click “acquire.”
Adjust forward and side scatter (FSC and SSC) to position the beads in a central position on the FSC and SSC plot.
Create a gate around the beads called P1.
Set cytometer to acquire 10,000 events within the P1 gate.
Click “record.”
Repeat the process for the FP-coupled beads.
Repeat step 7 for the unstained and FP-expressing cells.
Adjust FSC and SSC gain for unstained and FP-expressing cells.
Custom settings can be saved for beads and cells separately.
Right-click the statistics box to save these values as a CSV file.
Viewing a raw worksheet, create a statistics box including only the MFIs of all fluorescence channels and the parameter name.
Create a spreadsheet with parameter names in row 1.
Enter MFI values from blank beads in row 2.
Enter MFI values from FP-coupled beads in row 3.
Calculate corrected MFIs by subtracting blank-bead MFIs from FP-bead MFIs in row 4.
Normalize CMFI values by dividing each value in row 4 by the highest value in row 4.
Create a scatter plot with fluorescence channel on the x-axis and normalized CMFI on the y-axis.
Repeat step for unstained cells.
Repeat step for FP-expressing cells.
Calculate differences between normalized CMFIs of cells and beads for each channel.
Determine sum of these differences, referred to as difference index (DI).
Normalize the DI by dividing the DI value by the DI value of beads that share little spectral similarity.
Use CFP- and mCherry-coupled beads for comparison to produce a corrected difference index (CDI).
Resuspend the blank beads by inverting the bottle multiple times or vortexing vigorously.
Dispense one drop of blank beads into a 12 × 75–mm test tube (∼40 µl).
Add 200 µl DPBS to the test tube with blank beads.
Repeat step for each of the FP-coupled bead types.
Add 200 µl unstained cells to a 12 × 75–mm test tube (∼50,000 cells).
Create an experiment in SpectroFlo and select the fluorochromes used in the experiment.
Run the unstained cells and then each of the reference controls.
Select “unmix,” click “next,” and choose the “QC controls” tab.
Select the “similarity matrix” button and then select “View Similarity Matrix.”
Export the similarity matrix.
Open FlowJo software and use “add samples” to import all reference-control FCS files.
Drag the single FP–coupled beads and the blank beads onto the Compensation group.
Open the compensation tool.
Display the compensation matrix.
Click on the “SSM” button and choose “export SSM.”
Generate a CSV file from the export process.
Open the resulting CSV file in Microsoft Excel or another graphing software.
